OS-level termination primitive + real Docker namespace sweep, wrapped as the supervised entrypoint scripts/run_supervised.py. 6 unit tests prove termination (a SIGTERM-trapping child is still killed by SIGKILL; a group kill reaches a grandchild). 2 Docker-gated integration tests prove the sweep against REAL containers: the sweep removes an autosut container, and a hung run that created a container is terminated by its process group and its container swept (residual empty). This is genuine termination, unlike the in-process watchdog whose thread.join is race-mitigation only. This level is bounded: integration_tested reflects the PRIMITIVE + sweep proven against a real Docker dependency, NOT the canonical experiment path. Promotion is evidence-gated, never automatic. One happy-path supervised full caldera run IS now recorded under run_supervised.py (9/9 stages ok, effect confirmed, final_state clean, residual none, supervisor exit 0 with escalation=[], sweep empty) -- but escalation=[] means no signal fired, so that run validates the WRAPPER, not termination. Termination on REAL experiment stages, and R4 resolution, require the structured cross-stage interruption matrix (materialize/readiness/provision/sandcat/enroll/operation/persist/teardown x SIGINT,SIGTERM,deadline) with clean residual inventory. That matrix is not yet run, and the qualifying batches do not yet route exclusively through run_supervised.py, so R4 is integration-proven-on-Docker, NOT resolved.

Native Windows is an active but unqualified development track. The current source includes a credential-free unattended template, a per-run renderer, and host preflight checks; no native Windows guest boot, procedure execution, teardown, or independent reproduction has passed. The corpus question is controlled by the hash-bound human-adjudication protocol in docs/NATIVE_WINDOWS_CORPUS_ADJUDICATION.md: ATT&CK platform labels only triage review packets and cannot determine semantics. Until a frozen vendored corpus, complete protocol-defined adjudication, and separate execution qualification exist, this capability is not qualified and cannot support a claim.

Ran against the persistent dev Caldera, not a per-run isolated instance, so not promoted to end_to_end_validated.

A fresh Caldera is materialized on its own port, answers its API (ready in ~12s), yields its randomized red key, and is force-removed with confirmed absence -- all timed.
